claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified now because aggregate readiness passed and no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, with the limitation handled through model-card disclosure and post-launch monitoring.
specific_concerns: The enterprise refund workflow segment misses target by 1.8 points and is named in a renewal success plan, which is evidence of potential materiality.
Policy states material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required is still open, so a key policy predicate is unresolved.
No admissible evidence shows the model card already includes the required disclosure.
No admissible evidence shows an approved pre-launch risk acceptance covering the gap.
Product's 'non-core' characterization does not resolve materiality under the stated policy text.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant on the existing record.
That the disclosure condition has been satisfied.
That active monitoring alone is sufficient without resolved disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
That the product non-core framing meaningfully resolves the materiality dispute.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the enterprise refund workflow gap must be disclosed.
The current model card or release artifact showing the limitation is explicitly disclosed.
Approved pre-launch risk acceptance if disclosure will not be completed before launch.
Evidence that the affected workflow is or is not a named launch use case under the release policy.
Any signed release decision documenting how the named-segment gap was dispositioned.
decision_criteria: If the limitation is explicitly disclosed in the model card before launch, certification becomes more supportable.
If there is approved pre-launch risk acceptance covering the gap, certification becomes more supportable even if the gap remains.
If legal confirms no disclosure is required and that conclusion is documented, concern decreases.
If neither disclosure nor approved risk acceptance exists at launch, certification would be noncompliant under the stated policy.
